title: Efficient Tree-based Parallel Algorithms for N-Body Simulations Using C++ Standard Parallelism
problem: N-body simulations using the Barnes-Hut approximation reduce complexity from O(N²) to O(N log N) through spatial hierarchies, but tree-based algorithms are inherently irregular, making performance-portable parallel implementations on multi-core CPUs and GPUs fundamentally challenging.
motivation: Performance-portable implementations of irregular algorithms are essential for scientific computing across diverse hardware platforms.
method: Two parallel strategies implement Barnes-Hut: an unbalanced concurrent octree and a balanced bounding volume hierarchy sorted by Hilbert spacefilling curve. Both use portable ISO C++ standard parallel algorithms with atomic primitives for synchronization, trading off different levels of GPU and CPU support to achieve competitive performance.
key_novelty: Demonstrating C++ Standard Parallelism execution policies (particularly par) effectively optimize irregular tree-based algorithms across heterogeneous CPUs and GPUs.
contributions: Two portable fully-parallel Barnes-Hut implementation strategies with GPU and CPU performance trade-offs
Evidence that par execution policy outperforms par_unseq on CPUs and GPUs with independent thread scheduling
Competitive performance demonstrations across multi-core CPUs and various GPU architectures
limitations: Specific scalability metrics, detailed performance analysis, and comprehensive comparisons with other N-body simulation frameworks not discussed.
primary_theme: Performance-portable tree-based parallelism for N-body simulations
